rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim says the verse was revealed after a man had relations with a non-maḥram woman short of intercourse.
rows.anchor: سبب نزولها ما في صحيح مسلم من حديث الرجل الذي عالج امرأة أجنبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the verse predated the incident and the Prophet applied it to that man; when asked whether it was only for him, he said it was for everyone.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت قبل ذلك، واستعملها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في قصة هذا الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the Prophet directly in commands to do good, while directing prohibitions to the community, is a mark of eloquence.
rows.anchor: حيث كان بأفعال الخير توجه الخطاب إليه، وحيث كان النهي عن المحظورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded prayer is the obligatory prayer; إقامة means maintaining it continuously, performing it fully, or performing it at its best times.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن المأمور بإقامتها هي الصلوات المكتوبة، وإقامتها دوامها، وقيل: أداؤها على تمامها، وقيل: فعلها في أفضل أوقاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طرفي النهار is an adverbial accusative; because each طرف belongs to the thing it bounds, the apparent referents are dawn and afternoon.
rows.anchor: فالذي يظهر أنهما الصبح والعصر، لأنهما طرفا النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fasting rule that dawn belongs to daytime supports dawn as one boundary: deliberate eating or intercourse after dawn invalidates the fast and entails makeup and expiation.
rows.anchor: على أن من أكل أو جامع بعد طلوع الفجر متعمدا أن يومه يوم فطر

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: They identify the two daytime prayers as dawn and ʿAṣr, and the night approaches as Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, leaving Ẓuhr outside this verse.
rows.anchor: وممن قال: هما الصبح والعصر الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، وقال: الزلف المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومحمد بن كعب
rows.claim: They assign the first boundary to dawn and the second to Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, with Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at night; the passage says dawn is not included in this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومحمد بن كعب: الطرف الأول الصبح، والثاني الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: They identify the boundaries as dawn and Maghrib and the night prayer as ʿIshāʾ, excluding Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن أيضا: هما الصبح والمغرب، والزلف العشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr as the boundaries and dawn, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ as night prayers, apparently grouping them by recitation aloud or quietly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هما الظهر والعصر، والزلف المغرب والعشاء والصبح، وكأن هذا القائل راعى

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās’s dawn-and-Maghrib interpretation; Abū Ḥayyān objects that Maghrib belongs to night, so calling it a daytime boundary requires metaphor.
rows.anchor: ورجح الطبري قول ابن عباس: وهو أن الطرفين هما الصبح والمغرب، ولا نجعل المغرب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes dawn as the morning prayer, Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr as afternoon prayers, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ as the night approaches.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: غدوة وعشية قال: وصلاة الغدوة الصبح، وصلاة العشية الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the period after noon ʿashiyy does not make Ẓuhr a boundary, since the command names the day's two boundaries rather than morning and afternoon.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم من إطلاق العشي على ما بعد الزوال أن يكون الظهر طرفا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read zulafan with an open lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وزلفا بفتح اللام، وطلحة وعيسى البصرة

rows.speaker: طلحة وعيسى البصرة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers use a damma on the lām, as though the word were a singular noun.
rows.anchor: وطلحة وعيسى البصرة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر: بضمها كأنه اسم مفرد

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن ومجاهد
rows.claim: They read the lām quiescent; a further transmission from them has zulfa on the fuʿlā pattern, a feminine singular meaning a station or degree.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن ومجاهد: بإسكانها، وروي عنهما: وزلفى على وزن فعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural readings treat the word as successive stations or as a collective noun; zulafā is equivalent to one zalfa.
rows.anchor: فزلف جمع كظلم، وزلف كبسر في بسر، وزلف كبسر في بسرة، فهما اسما جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax coordinates the night approaches with the two daytime boundaries as another bounded period.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عطف وزلفا من الليل على طرفي النهار، عطف طرفا على طرف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains zulaf as the part of the day near nightfall; another interpretation makes it night prayers of devotion and coordinates it with الصلاة instead.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقد ذكر هذه القراآت وهو ما يقرب من آخر النهار من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasanāt can mean all good deeds, especially obligatory prayers and Ramadan fasting; sayyiʾāt in this reading means minor sins, as supported by the sound report about avoiding major sins.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عموم الحسنات من الصلوات المفروضة، وصيام رمضان، وما أشبههما من فرائض الإسلام. وخصوص السيئات وهي الصغائر

rows.speaker: جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين
rows.claim: Most early interpreters identify the good deeds specifically as the five prayers; Mālik adopts this interpretation, and ʿUthmān illustrates it while performing ablution.
rows.anchor: وذهب جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين: إلى أن الحسنات يراد بها الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the good deeds as the formulas of remembrance: glorifying and praising God, proclaiming his oneness and greatness, and declaring reliance on him.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الحسنات قول الرجل: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These interpretations should be understood as examples; the five prayers are the greatest deeds.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يحمل هذا كله على جهة المثال في الحساب، ومن أجل أن الصلوات الخمس هي أعظم الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minor sins are erased only when one repents and does not persist in them, a position stated explicitly by the most discerning legal theorists.
rows.anchor: والصغائر التي تذهب هي بشرط التوبة منها وعدم الإصرار عليها، وهذا نص حذاق الأصوليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Erasing sins means expiating minor sins, not making past acts cease to have happened.
rows.anchor: ومعنى إذهابها: تكفير الصغائر، والصغائر قد وجدت وأذهبت الحسنات ما كان يترتب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that good deeds graciously help people leave sins rather than erase sins already committed, as prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى إن فعل الحسنات يكون لطفا في ترك السيئات، لا أنها واقعة كقوله: إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative ذلك most apparently points to the nearest command: establishing prayer at these times as a reminder for those who take heed.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الإشارة قوله ذلك، إلى أقرب مذكور وهو قوله: أقم الصلاة أي إقامتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other referents for ذلك are the news that good deeds erase sins, earlier commands and prohibitions, or the Qurʾān; al-Zamakhsharī gives the earlier counsel as his view and al-Ṭabarī points to this sūrah's commands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إشارة إلى الإخبار بأن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات، فيكون في هذه الذكرى حضا على فعل الحسنات

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the implied sense as there having been no people of remaining virtue, making the exception connected despite its apparent form.
rows.anchor: يراه منفيا من حيث معناه: أنه لم يكن فيهم أولو بقية، ولهذا قال الزمخشري بعد أن منع

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads قليل in the nominative because the exhortation implies a negation, permitting substitution as after an explicit negative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: إلا قليل بالرفع، لحظ أن التحضيض تضمن النفي، فأبدل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the implied meaning is they did not do so, since a question carries a shade of negation.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى فلم يكن، لأن في الاستفهام ضربا من الجحد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash rejects treating the exception as disconnected.
rows.anchor: وأبى الأخفش كون الاستثناء منقطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wrongdoers are those who abandoned forbidding corruption.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الذين ظلموا هم تاركو النهي عن الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly enjoyment means the love of leadership and wealth and pursuit of a comfortable life, at the expense of religious good.
rows.anchor: وما أترفوا فيه أي: ما نعموا فيه من حب الرياسة والثروة وطلب أسباب العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next clause reports that these wrongdoers, despite abandoning the prohibition of corruption, were also criminals in other ways.
rows.anchor: واتبع استئناف إخبار عن حال هؤلاء الذين ظلموا، وإخبار عنهم أنهم مع كونهم تاركي النهي عن الفساد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses followed desires as coordinated with an implied clause about the few who were saved and the wrongdoers who followed desires; alternatively, it describes their punishment as a circumstance.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: إن كان معناه واتبعوا الشهوات كان معطوفا على مضمر، لأن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ما أترفوا فيه favors reading ما as a relative pronoun, since فيه refers back to it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها بمعنى الذي لعود الضمير في فيه عليها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows وكانوا مجرمين to coordinate with اتبعوا or to be a judgment on them.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أيضا أن يكون معطوفا على اتبعوا أي: اتبعوا شهواتهم وكانوا مجرمين بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the final judgment an اعتراض is technically inaccurate because it closes the verse rather than interrupting two syntactically dependent parts.
rows.anchor: ولا يسمى هذا اعتراضا في اصطلاح النحو، لأنه آخر آية، فليس بين شيئين يحتاج

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد والعلاء بن سيابة وأبو عمر
rows.claim: They read passive وأتبعوا with a still tāʾ, understood with an omitted object as being made to follow the recompense of their luxury.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد، والعلاء بن سيابة كذا في كتاب اللوامح، وأبو عمر في رواية الجعفي: وأتبعوا ساكنة التاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows the common active reading to mean that they followed the recompense for their luxury; the prior mention of salvation supports the sense that everyone else perished.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى في القراءة المشهورة أنهم اتبعوا جزاء إترافهم، وهذا معنى قوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a kasra, niswah is a broken plural of limited number with no singular of the same form; Ibn al-Sarrāj instead calls it a collective noun.
rows.anchor: النسوة بكسر النون فعلة، وهو جمع تكسير للقلة لا واحد له من لفظه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls niswah a singular collective noun for women and says the feminine ending on the verb is unnecessary because its grammatical femininity is not real.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: النسوة اسم مفرد لجمع المرأة، وتأنيثه غير حقيقي، ولذا لم تلحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān replies that a broken plural need not take a feminine verb ending, as both genders are possible with collective plurals such as Hind.
rows.anchor: وعلى أنه جمع تكسير لا يلحق التاء لأنه يجوز: قامت الهنود، وقام الهنود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a damma on its nūn the form is a collective noun; niswān and al-nisāʾ are large broken plurals without a singular of the same form.
rows.anchor: وقد تضم نونه فتكون إذ ذاك اسم جمع، وتكسيره للكثرة على نسوان، والنساء جمع تكسير للكثرة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaghafa is described as piercing the heart's covering, reaching its core, or as an illness entering the heart; Tamīm also pronounces its ghayn with kasra.
rows.anchor: شغف: خرق الشغاف، وهو حجاب القلب. وقيل: سويداؤه، وقيل: داء يصل إلى القلب فينفذ إلى القلب. وكسر الغين لغة تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another lexical explanation calls the shighāf a thin layer, the heart's tongue; being love-struck is likened to a camel burned by tar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الشغاف جلدة رقيقة يقال لها لسان القلب، شغف وصلت الحدة إلى القلب

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse uses al-mashghūf for one whose heart love has burned, illustrating the word's passion sense.
rows.anchor: والمشغوف الذي أحرق الحب قلبه. ومنه قول الأعشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muttaqaʾ is explained as a cushion or small pillow.
rows.anchor: المتكأ: الوسادة، والنمرقة. المتك: الأترج، والواحد متكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutk may mean citron, and a poetic line describes a gift of it; it may also name any fruit cut with a knife.
rows.anchor: فأهدت متكة لهي أبيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poetic line supports mutk as something cut; the proposed root is mataka, meaning to cut.
rows.anchor: وهو من متك بمعنى بتك الشيء أي قطعه

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl says mutk with ḍamma means honey; al-Aṣmaʿī says it means citron.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح: المتك بالضم عند الخليل العسل، وعند الأصمعي الأترج

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr gives pure drink as a meaning, and reports three vowelings; kasra may mean a toothpick or musk.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمر: والشراب الخالص. وقال أبو عمر: وفيه ثلاث لغات، المتك بالحركات الثلاث

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī also allows all three vowelings, with meanings including a brazier, a sweet, or a wrapped meat-and-bread dish.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي أيضا: فيه اللغات الثلاث، وقد يكون بالفتح المجمر عند قضاعة

rows.speaker: الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Faḍl says the term can mean bazmāward, a dish of meat wrapped in thin bread.
rows.anchor: وقال الفضل: في اللغات الثلاث هو البزماورد، وكل ملفوف بلحم ورقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further reported meanings of mutk with ḍamma include a table or, in Kinda, wine.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا: المتك بالضم المائدة، أو الخمر في لغة كندة

rows.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī say sikkīn can be masculine or feminine; al-Aṣmaʿī recognizes only masculine.
rows.anchor: السكين: تذكر وتؤنث، قاله الفراء والكسائي. ولم يعرف الأصمعي فيه إلا التذكير

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says some Arabs lengthen ḥāshā; in the Hijaz it is ḥāshā laka, while others say ḥashiya Zayd, with an implied preposition.
rows.anchor: حاش: قال الفراء من العرب من يتمها، وفي لغة الحجاز: حاش لك، وبعض العرب: حشى زيد

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī explains ittekaʾnā as eating, a metonym for the reclining posture of the wealthy; the Prophet said he does not eat reclining.
rows.anchor: قال القتبي: يقال اتكأنا عند فلان أي أكلنا، ويكون هذا من المجاز عبر بالهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If muttaqaʾ does not itself mean food, the gathering still entails food and drink, including items cut with knives.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان المتكأ ليس معبرا به عما يؤكل، فمعلوم أن مثل هذا المجلس لا بد فيه من طعام وشراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported foods included meat eaten in slices, citron, bazmāward, and a confection of sugar, almonds, and mixtures, all cut with a knife.
rows.anchor: فقيل: كان لحما وكانوا لا ينهشون اللحم، إنما كانوا يأكلونه حزا بالسكاكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women's knives could make them cut their hands while distracted and then shame them; the scene could also frighten Joseph with a group of women holding blades.
rows.anchor: قيل: وكان قصدها في بروزهن على هذه الهيئات متكئات في أيديهن سكاكين يحززن بها شيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spectacle may have been meant to keep Joseph afraid of her plot, though God protected him from the evil she intended.
rows.anchor: فيكون يحذر مكرها دائما. ولعله يجيبها إلى مرادها على زعمها ذلك

rows.speaker: الزهري وأبو جعفر وشيبة
rows.claim: They read muttaki with doubled tāʾ and no hamza, either by easing the hamza in the form for reclining or deriving it from binding or cutting.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري، وأبو جعفر، وشيبة: متكي مشدد التاء من غير همز بوزن متقي

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads mutkaʾ as a form from takaʾa, to recline.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج: متكئا مفعلا من تكأ يتكأ إذا اتكأ

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن هرمز
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Hurmuz read mutkāʾ with lengthened alif and hamza, from reclining with an expanded vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وابن هرمز: متكاء بالمد والهمز، وهو مفتعل من الاتكاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والجحدري والكلبي وإبان بن تغلب
rows.claim: These readers give muttakaʾ a ḍamma on mīm, a still tāʾ, and tanwīn on kāf; Ibn Hurmuz is also reported with it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، وابن عمر، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك، والجحدري، والكلبي، وإبان بن تغلب: متكئا

rows.speaker: عبد الله ومعاذ
rows.claim: They use the same reading but with a fatḥa on mīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ومعاذ، وكذلك إلا أنهما فتحا الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command for Joseph to come out is addressed to him; his leaving shows her compliance in something that did not involve disobedience, with the exit itself elided.
rows.anchor: وقالت: اخرج عليهن، هذا الخطاب ليوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akbarnahu means they regarded him as magnificent and were astonished by his extraordinary beauty.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أكبرنه: أعظمنه ودهشن برؤية ذلك الجمال الفائق الرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report compares Joseph's beauty among people to the full moon among the stars.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان فضل يوسف على الناس في الحسن كفضل القمر ليلة البدر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report about the Night Journey, the Prophet compares Joseph's appearance to the full moon.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث الإسراء أن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أخبر بلقيا يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports say Joseph's face shone on the walls as he walked, that he resembled Adam at creation, or that he inherited beauty from Sarah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان إذا سار في أزقة مصر يرى تلألؤ وجهه على الجدران

rows.speaker: عبد الصمد بن علي الهاشمي
rows.claim: Abd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī al-Hāshimī, citing his father and grandfather, explains akbarnahu as menstruation and adduces a woman's verse.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الصمد بن علي الهاشمي، عن أبيه، عن جده: معناه حضن

rows.speaker: ابن عطية والطبري وغيرهم من المحققين
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and other critical scholars call the menstruation explanation weak and its supporting verse fabricated, noting Abd al-Ṣamad was not a reliable transmitter of knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا قول ضعيف، والبيت مصنوع مختلق، كذلك قال الطبري

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also reports that akbarnahu can mean menstruated, treating the hāʾ as a pause marker and deriving the sense from reaching maturity.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقيل أكبرن بمعنى حضن، والهاء للسكت يقال: أكبرت المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciters' agreement to pronounce the hāʾ with ḍamma in connected speech shows it is not a pause hāʾ; on that reading it refers to Joseph, while the hāʾ can represent the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وإجماع القراء على ضم الهاء في الوصل دليل على أنها ليست هاء السكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting the hands means wounding them; the intensive form reflects many women cutting or repeated cuts on each woman's hand while she was unaware.
rows.anchor: وقطعن أيديهن أي جرحنها، كما تقول: كنت أقطع اللحم فقطعت يدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of hands is the bodily limbs bearing that name.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأيدي هي الجوارح المسماة بهذا الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line is cited as evidence for the phrase describing the scorpion's legs and tail knots.
rows.anchor: أعوذ بالله من العقراب ... الشائلات عقد الأذناب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ḥāshā li-llāh without a lengthened alif after shīn.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: حاش لله بغير ألف بعد الشين، ولله بلام الجر

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ḥāshā li-llāh with the preposition lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: حاشا لله بغير ألف، ولام الجر

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: A group including al-Aʿmash reads ḥashiya with lām of preposition.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة منهم الأعمش: حشى على وزن رمى لله بلام الجر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ḥāsh with a still shīn in both connection and pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: حاش بسكون الشين وصلا، ووقفا بلام الجر

rows.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
rows.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read ḥāshā Allāh as an annexed form; another transmission from them matches Abū ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله: حاشى الله بالإضافة، وعنهما كقراءة أبي عمر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also reads ḥāsh al-ilāh; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it a shortened form, and the Lawāmiʿ author treats it as a preposition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: حاش الإله. قال ابن عطية: محذوفا من حاشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says those explanations do not prove the alif was deleted unless a pause reading is also reported; otherwise it may be elided to avoid adjacent still consonants.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله ابن عطية وصاحب اللوامح: من أن الألف في حاشى في قراءة الحسن محذوفة لا تتعين

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads ḥāshā li-llāh with tanwīn, like raʿyan li-llāh.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال: حاشا لله بالتنوين كرعيا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When لله has a prepositional lām, the preceding ḥāsh form cannot itself be a preposition, because two prepositions would collide and deletion is unusual for particles.
rows.anchor: فأما القراآت لله بلام الجر في غير قراءة أبي السمال فلا يجوز

rows.speaker: المبرد وابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and Ibn ʿAṭiyya say ḥāsh is a verb with Joseph as subject: he kept away from what the women accused him of.
rows.anchor: وزعم المبرد وغيره كابن عطية: أنه يتعين فعليتها، ويكون الفاعل ضمير يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the verbal analysis, li-llāh means for God's obedience, because of God's standing, or to exalt God above the accusation; the lām gives a causal sense.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لله: لطاعة الله، أو لمكانة من الله، أو لترفيع الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes ḥāsh a noun, a verbal noun replacing its verb, meaning declaring God free of the accusation; the tanwīn reading supports this.
rows.anchor: وذهب غير المبرد إلى أنها اسم، وانتصابها انتصاب المصدر الواقع بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the noun analysis, Allāh is linked to an omitted explanatory phrase, while common readings retain the particle's original indeclinable form, like ʿan.
rows.anchor: ويدل على اسميتها قراءة أبي السمال حاشا منونا، وعلى هذا القول يتعلق الله

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the hands as sleeves.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: الأيدي هنا الأكمام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī chooses to understand the ḍamma and annexed readings as a verbal noun annexed to God, like subḥān Allāh.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الحسن وقراءة أبي بالإضافة فهو مصدر مضاف إلى ألفه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, citing Abū ʿAlī, treats Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd's reading as an exception particle and supports it with a poetic line.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وأما قراءة أبي بن كعب وابن مسعود فقال أبو علي: إن حاشى حرف استثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The still-shīn reading attributed to al-Ḥasan joins two still consonants, a construction grammarians regard as weak.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الحسن حاش بالتسكين ففيها جمع بين ساكنين، وقد ضعفوا ذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says ḥāshā li-llāh marvels at God's power to create extraordinary beauty, while the women's later words marvel at creating chastity.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والمعنى تنزيه الله من صفات العجز، والتعجب من قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women denied Joseph's humanity because his beauty exceeded ordinary human beauty and affirmed angelhood, since people instinctively imagine angels as beautiful though unseen.
rows.anchor: ما هذا بشرا لما كان غريب الجمال فائق الحسن عما عليه حسن صور الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic poets likewise compare exceptional beauty to angels.
rows.anchor: وقد نطق بذلك شعراء العرب والمحدثون قال بعض العرب: فلست لإنسي ولكن لملأك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative بشر follows Hijazi grammar; other Qurʾānic examples show the same construction, while Tamīm uses the nominative.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب بشرا على لغة الحجاز، ولذا جاء: ما هن أمهاتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the nominative form was not read.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولم يقرأ به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says a Tamīm speaker using his dialect would say بشر in the nominative; he identifies Ibn Masʿūd's reading with it.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومن قرأ على سليقته من بني تميم قرأ بشر بالرفع

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو الحويرث الحنفي
rows.claim: They read بشرى, which may mean Joseph is not merchandise for sale or purchase, nor something with a price, but is too exalted for that.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو الحويرث الحنفي: ما هذا بشرى، قال صاحب اللوامح

rows.speaker: عبد الوارث عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Wārith also reports this reading from Abū ʿAmr and adds إلا ملك with a kasra, placing Joseph among kings rather than enslaved people.
rows.anchor: وتابعهما عبد الوارث عن أبي عمرو على ذلك، وزاد عليهما: إلا ملك بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women point out that Joseph, whose beauty made them deny he was human and call him an angel, is the one for whom they blamed her.
rows.anchor: الذي قطعتن أيديكن بسببه وأكبرتنه وقلتن فيه ما قلتن من نفي البشرية عنه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the demonstrative could refer to the Canaanite servant they had imagined; seeing Joseph as he really is should make them excuse her infatuation.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون إشارة إلى المعنى بقولهن: عشقت عبدها الكنعاني

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows the demonstrative to point to Joseph's love, with the pronoun referring to love rather than Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويجوز أن تكون الإشارة إلى حب يوسف، والضمير عائد على الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife then admitted to the women that she had tried to seduce Joseph, trusting that they now excused her.
rows.anchor: ثم أقرت امرأة العزيز للنسوة بالمراودة، واستنامت إليهن في ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya glosses istaʿṣama as seeking and holding fast to protection, and resisting her.
rows.anchor: فاستعصم قال ابن عطية: معناه طلب العصمة، وتمسك بها وعصاني

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes istaʿṣama as an intensive pattern expressing powerful refusal and guardedness, as if Joseph were already protected but strove for more.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والاستعصام بناء مبالغة يدل على الامتناع البليغ والتحفظ الشديد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats Joseph's refusal as a clear proof against interpretations that attribute sinful desire to him.
rows.anchor: وهذا بيان لما كان من يوسف عليه السلام لا مزيد عليه، وبرهان لا شيء أنور منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the grammarians' analysis: istaʿṣama matches iʿtaṣama and denotes actual protection, not seeking it or a special intensification.
rows.anchor: والذي ذكر التصريفيون في استعصم أنه موافق لاعتصم، فاستفعل فيه موافق لافتعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogies cited for intensification also match the iftiʿāl pattern; istafḥala instead matches tafaʿʿala.
rows.anchor: وأما استمسك واستوسع واستجمع الرأي فاستفعل فيه موافقة لافتعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first object of آمر is omitted, with the sense that she commands Joseph to do something; if ما is a verbal noun, its pronoun instead returns to Joseph.
rows.anchor: ومفعول آمر الأول محذوف، وكان التقدير ما آمره به

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group reads وليكونن with a doubled nūn; the written alif reflects the majority's light nūn reading and remains in pausal spelling, as in al-Aʿshā's verse.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: وليكونن بالنون المشددة، وكتبها في المصحف بالألف مراعاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣāghirīn means the humiliated.
rows.anchor: ومن الصاغرين: من الأذلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She threatened painful punishment in the earlier scene while still angry and denying her pursuit; now she is hopeful, has justified herself to the women, and threatens prison instead.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر هنا العذاب الأليم الذي ذكرته في ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women urge Joseph to obey, framing compliance as preferable to imprisonment and humiliation; his answer attributes the call to them because they counsel and adorn compliance.
rows.anchor: وقال له النسوة: أطع وافعل ما أمرتك به، فقال: رب السجن أحب إلي

rows.speaker: عثمان ومولاه طارق وزيد بن علي والزهري وابن أبي إسحاق وابن هرمز ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce sijn with an open sīn as the verbal noun of imprisonment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عثمان، ومولاه طارق، وزيد بن علي، والزهري، وابن أبي إسحاق، وابن هرمز، ويعقوب: السجن بفتح السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥabb is not a true comparison: Joseph chooses the lesser of two evils, rejecting sinful pleasure for hardship in God's cause, patience, and prayer for relief.
rows.anchor: وأحب هنا ليست على بابها من التفضيل، لأنه لم يحب ما يدعونه إليه قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph entrusts protection to God and submits, as prophets and the righteous do, since only God averts evil.
rows.anchor: ثم ناط العصمة بالله، واستسلم لله كعادة الأنبياء والصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣbu indicates inclination alone, not committing the forbidden act.
rows.anchor: وجعل جواب الشرط قوله: أصب، وهي كلمة مشعرة بالميل فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant derives aṣib from ṣabāba, intense longing that pours toward what one desires.
rows.anchor: وقرىء أصب إليهن من صببت صبابة فأنا صب، والصبابة إفراط الشوق

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority derive aṣbu from ṣabā, to turn toward amusement or play; ṣibā with kasra means play.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور: أصب من صبا إلى اللهو يصبو صبا وصبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jāhilīn can mean people whose knowledge produces no benefit or foolish people, since yielding to the women's invitation would be folly; a poem supports the latter sense.
rows.anchor: وأكن من الجاهلين من الذين يعملون بما، لأن من لا جدوى لعلمه فهو ومن لا يعلم سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response to Joseph's prayer has no preceding explicit الدعاء because وإلا تصرف عني already implies a request: Lord, avert their plot.
rows.anchor: وذكر استجابة الله له ولم يتقدم لفظ دعاء لأن قوله: وإلا تصرف عني، فيه معنى طلب الصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's diversion of the plot means he prevented Joseph from sin; God hears those who seek refuge and knows their inner states.
rows.anchor: فصرف عنه كيدهن أي: حال بينه وبين المعصية. إنه هو السميع لدعاء الملتجئين إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badā means became apparent; Abū Ḥayyān prefers an understood subject referring to imprisonment, understood from the threat or the word sijn.
rows.anchor: والذي أذهب إليه أن الفاعل ضمير يعود على السجن المفهوم من قوله: ليسجنن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians and commentators usually posit an implicit subject explained by the context; another grammatical view makes the clause about imprisonment the subject, which Abū Ḥayyān rejects.
rows.anchor: هكذا قاله النحاة والمفسرون، إلا من أجاز أن تكون الجملة فاعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in لهم refers to the ʿAzīz and his household; the signs are proofs of Joseph's innocence.
rows.anchor: والضمير في لهم للعزيز وأهله، والآيات هي: الشواهد الدالة على براءة يوسف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and others identify the shirt's tear as a sign; if the witness was an infant this was miraculous, while a grown witness would indicate innocence by ordinary inference.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وغيره: قد القميص، فإن كان الشاهد طفلا فهي آية عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says āyāt refers to clear evidence and its plural indicates several manifest proofs, perhaps including unmentioned evidence and the witness's statement.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن الآية إنما يعبر بها عن الواضح الجلي، وجمعها يدل على ظهور أمور

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima's report that the signs included scratches on her face does not establish Joseph's innocence and is not a proof.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذكره عكرمة أن من الآيات خمش وجهها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī's report that the signs included cuts on the women's hands does not establish Joseph's innocence and is not a proof.
rows.anchor: والسدي من حز أيديهن، فليس في ذلك دلالة على البراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layusjunannahu answers an unspoken oath within quoted speech; al-Ḥasan's tāʾ reading addresses the ʿAzīz or respectfully addresses his circle.
rows.anchor: وليسجننه جواب قسم محذوف والقسم وجوابه معمول لقول محذوف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads with a tāʾ, addressing the ʿAzīz's circle or the ʿAzīz alone as a form of respect.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: لتسجننه بالتاء على خطاب بعضهم العزيز ومن يليه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads ʿattā, replacing the ḥāʾ of ḥattā with ʿayn, a Hudhayl dialect; he was instructed to teach Quraysh usage instead.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: عتى بإبدال حاء حتى عينا، وهي لغة هذيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥīn denotes an unspecified time; any particular duration assigned here derives from Joseph's prison term, not the word's lexical meaning.
rows.anchor: والحين يدل على مطلق الوقت، ومن عين له هنا زمانا فإنما كان ذلك باعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed term in prison was a period in which they could see how Joseph behaved.
rows.anchor: وكأنها اقترحت زمانا حتى تبصر ما يكون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imprisonment illustrates women's plotting and a husband who yields authority to his wife despite her treachery and Joseph's innocence.
rows.anchor: وفي سجنهم ليوسف دليل على مكيدة النساء، واستنزال المرأة لزوجها ومطاوعته لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the ʿAzīz's wife told her husband that the Hebrew boy had defamed her, asking either to defend herself publicly or to be imprisoned as she was.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما امتنع يوسف من المعصية، ويئست منه امرأة العزيز قالت لزوجها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Joseph was carried on a donkey through Egyptian markets as a drum announced that he had sought his mistress and deserved prison.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فأمر به فحمل على حمار، وضرب بالطبل، ونودي عليه في أسواق مصر

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says Ibn ʿAbbās wept whenever he told this account.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح: ما ذكر ابن عباس هذا الحديث إلا بكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text elides their imprisonment of Joseph before saying that two young men entered prison with him.
rows.anchor: في الكلام حذف تقديره: فسجنوه، فدخل معه السجن غلامان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report identifies the young men as the king al-Walīd ibn al-Rayyān's baker and cupbearer.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهما كانا للملك الأعظم الوليد بن الريان، أحدهما خبازه، والآخر ساقيه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the king suspected the baker of trying to poison him and the cupbearer of consenting, and jailed both.
rows.anchor: فسجنهما قاله: السدي. ومع تدل على الصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word مع indicates co-presence and a new shared event, so all three were imprisoned at the same time.
rows.anchor: ومع تدل على الصحبة واستحداثها، فدل على أنهم سجنوا الثلاثة في ساعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In prison Joseph comforted the grieving, visited the ill, advocated for the poor, urged goodness, and won the affection of prisoners and the keeper.
rows.anchor: ولما دخل يوسف السجن استمال الناس بحسن حديثه وفضله ونبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the keeper offered Joseph his choice of rooms, Joseph said not to love him because love had brought him trials through his aunt, father, and the ʿAzīz's wife.
rows.anchor: وقال له: كن في أي البيوت شئت فقال له يوسف: لا تحبني يرحمك الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph told the prisoners that he was skilled at interpreting dreams.
rows.anchor: وكان يوسف عليه السلام قد قال لأهل السجن: إني أعبر الرؤيا وأجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two young men said they loved Joseph from their first sight of him; he adjured them not to love him and repeated the trials love had brought.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الفتيين قالا له: إنا لنحبك من حين رأيناك فقال: أنشدكما الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says Joseph encouraged despondent inmates to be patient and hopeful of reward; they praised his character and asked who he was.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: كان في السجن ناس قد انقطع رجاؤهم وطال حزنهم، فجعل يقول: اصبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph introduces himself as Jacob, God's chosen, son of Isaac, God's sacrificed one, son of Abraham, God's friend; the prison keeper says he would free him if able.
rows.anchor: قال يوسف: ابن صفي الله يعقوب، ابن ذبيح الله إسحاق ابن خليل الله إبراهيم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the two men truly saw these dreams and wanted to ask Joseph about them.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: رأيا ذلك حقيقة فأرادا سؤاله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والشعبي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and al-Shaʿbī say the prisoners pretended to dream in order to test Joseph.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود والشعبي: استعملاها ليجرباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer, called Bunū, describes three grape clusters whose juice he pressed for the king.
rows.anchor: والذي رأى عصر الخمر اسمه بنو قال: رأيت حبلة من كرم لها ثلاثة أغصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The baker, called Malḥab, describes three baskets of bread carried on his head, from which birds ate.
rows.anchor: والذي رأى الخبز اسمه ملحب قال: كنت أرى أن أخرج من مطبخة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream verb is like verbs of cognition: its subject and object may be pronouns referring to the same person, though ordinary paired pronouns such as اضربني are disallowed.
rows.anchor: ورأى الحلمية جرت مجرى أفعال القلوب في جواز كون فاعلها ومفعولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grapes are called wine in anticipation of what they become; some dialects use khamr for grapes directly.
rows.anchor: وسمي العنب خمرا باعتبار ما يؤول إليه. وقيل: الخمر بلغة غسان اسم العنب

rows.speaker: المعتمر
rows.claim: Al-Muʿtamir recounts asking a Bedouin carrying grapes what he had; the man answered khamr, meaning grapes.
rows.anchor: وقال المعتمر: لقيت أعرابيا يحمل عنبا في وعاء فقلت: ما تحمل؟ قال: خمرا

rows.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
rows.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read عنبا, but Abū Ḥayyān treats it as an explanatory gloss, since their transmitted mutawātir reading is خمرا and the form conflicts with the codex text.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله: أعصر عنبا، وينبغي أن يحمل ذلك على التفسير لمخالفته سواد المصحف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows khamr to be described as pressed because pressing is done for its sake.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويجوز أن يكون وصف الخمر بأنها معصورة، إذ العصر لها ومن أجلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in ʿAbd Allāh's codex about tharīd is also an explanatory gloss, not a reading.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله: فوق رأسي ثريدا تأكل الطير منه، وهو أيضا تفسير لا قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in تأويله refers to everything the men related, functioning like a demonstrative meaning that.
rows.anchor: والضمير في تأويله عائد إلى ما قصا عليه، أجري مجرى اسم الإشارة كأنه قيل: بتأويل ذلك

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand محسنين as skilled in knowledge, since the two men saw that Joseph was learned.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: من المحسنين أي في العلم، لأنهما رأيا منه ما علما به أنه عالم

rows.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda understand محسنين as kind in speech and courteous to prison inmates.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وقتادة: من المحسنين في حديثه مع أهل السجن وإجماله معهم

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the men meant that Joseph had done them a kindness by interpreting their dreams.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: أرادا إخباره أنهما يريان له إحسانا عليهما ويدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph promises to tell the men what their food means in waking life before the foretold outcome appears.
rows.anchor: أنكما رزقتماه إلا أعلمتكما بتأويل ذلك الطعام أي: بما يؤول إليه أمره في اليقظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The men ask how Joseph claims such knowledge when he is neither a soothsayer nor astrologer; he replies that his Lord taught him.
rows.anchor: فروي أنهما قالا له: ومن أين لك ما تدعيه من العلم وأنت لست بكاهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reference is food received while awake, and saying his Lord taught him shows that Joseph was already a prophet receiving revelation.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: لا يأتيكما إلى آخره، أنه في اليقظة، وأن قوله: مما علمني ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph explains his creed to two men who had grown fond of him, so they can follow him; he says he left their religion even though he never adhered to it, using ترک as early avoidance.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: أني تركت، استئناف إخبار بما هو عليه، إذ كانا قد أحباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, his rejection of their religion and adoption of his prophetic forebears' monotheism explain why God taught and inspired him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون إني تركت تعليلا لما قبله أي: علمني ذلك، وأوحي إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are Egyptians and people sharing the prisoners' religion; the passage stresses belief in God and the afterlife as two foundational principles.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء الذين لا يؤمنون هم أهل مصر، ومن كان الفتيان على دينهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the repeated هم as restrictive: these Egyptians in particular deny the afterlife, unlike others, and their denial explains their injustice and grave sins.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وتكريرهم للدلالة على أنهم خصوصا كافرون بالآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says هم does not establish that restriction and calls the rest of al-Zamakhsharī's wording Muʿtazilī.
rows.anchor: وليست عندنا هم تدل على الخصوص، وباقي ألفاظه ألفاظ المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning his forefathers' religion establishes Joseph's prophetic lineage and reinforces the men's desire to listen and follow after his foreknowledge showed him a prophet.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر أنه رفض ملة أولئك ذكر اتباعه ملة آبائه ليريهما أنه من بيت النبوة

rows.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي والكوفيون
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī and the Kufans read آبائي with a still yāʾ, also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي والكوفيون: آبائي بإسكان الياء، وهي مروية عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is not fitting for prophets to associate anything with God, whether an idol, jinn, human, or any object; من is extra under negation and the noun can denote associating anything or association itself.
rows.anchor: ما كان لنا ما صح ولا استقام لنا معشر الأنبياء أن نشرك بالله من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to the pure monotheistic religion: God's favor to messengers is making them mediators, and his favor to people is guiding them to salvation.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بذلك إلى شركهم وملتهم أي: ذلك الدين والشرع الحنيفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged gods are only names invented by people and their ancestors, empty of real referents.
rows.anchor: ومعنى إلا أسماء: أي ألفاظا أحدثتموها أنتم وآباؤكم فهي فارغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God legislates worship and religion, not people or idols; al-qayyim means firmly established and supported by proofs.
rows.anchor: إن الحكم إلا لله أي: ليس لكم ولا لأصنامكم حكم ما الحكم في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fail to know this because ignorance and unbelief dominate them.
rows.anchor: لا يعلمون بجهالاتهم وغلبة الكفر عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After delivering the more important teaching about religion, Joseph calls the men his prison companions again so they will focus on the interpretation.
rows.anchor: لما ألقى إليهما ما كان أهم وهو أمر الدين رجاء في إيمانهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tells Bunū that he will return to his former post serving the king; three vine branches mean three more days in prison before release.
rows.anchor: فروي أنه قال: لبنو: أما أنت فتعود إلى مرتبتك وسقاية ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tells Malḥab that his three baskets mean three days until he is released and crucified.
rows.anchor: وقال لملحب: أما أنت فما رأيت من السلال ثلاثة أيام ثم تخرج فتصلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports say the men denied seeing anything because they had pretended to test Joseph; another says only the man told he would be crucified said this, while another says both saw and then denied it.
rows.anchor: فروي أنهما قالا: ما رأينا شيئا، وإنما تحالمنا لنجربك

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yasqī from saqā; another group reads yusqī from asqā, and both verbs can mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فيسقي ربه من سقى، وفرقة: فيسقي من أسقى، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The Lawāmiʿ author says saqā and asqā are synonyms, though the usual distinction is giving a drink versus providing water.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح: سقى وأسقى بمعنى واحد في اللغة، والمعروف أن سقاه

rows.speaker: عكرمة والجحدري
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Jaḥdarī read the passive yusqā, meaning that the king will be given wine to drink.
rows.anchor: ونسب ضم الفاء لعكرمة والجحدري،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya understands ربه as the prisoner's master.
rows.anchor: ونسب ضم الفاء لعكرمة والجحدري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph tells the prisoners through knowledge from God that the outcome is decreed whether their dreams were genuine or feigned.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبرهما يوسف عليه السلام عن غيب علمه من قبل الله أن الأمر قد قضي ووافق القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular الأمر refers to the final outcome of the accusation that jailed the men: one is saved and one killed.
rows.anchor: وأفرد الأمر وإن كان أمر هذا، لأن المقصود إنما هو عاقبة أمرهما

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda takes ẓann in its ordinary sense because dream interpretation is conjectural.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: الظن هنا على بابه، لأن عبارة الرؤيا ظن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes Joseph the one who thought the cupbearer would be released; Abū Ḥayyān says this is difficult if the interpretation came by conjecture because the decree is final, unless the phrase only means Joseph has finished speaking.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الظان هو يوسف عليه السلام إن كان تأويله بطريق الاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph may have asked the cupbearer to tell the king about his knowledge and standing, or to report his unjust imprisonment.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أن يوسف عليه السلام قال لساقي الملك حين علم أنه سيعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān sees Joseph's request as permissible practical help, with God making it a cause of relief; he compares it to Jesus seeking helpers and the Prophet seeking a guard.
rows.anchor: وهذا من يوسف على سبيل الاستعانة والتعاون في تفريج كربه، وجعله بإذن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers that Joseph wanted to lead the cupbearer to faith, as he had sought the guidance of both prisoners.
rows.anchor: والذي أختاره أن يوسف إنما قال لساقي الملك: اذكرني عند ربك ليتوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فأنساه refers to the cupbearer; ذكر ربه means remembering Joseph for his master, and the loose relation permits the possessive.
rows.anchor: والضمير في فأنساه عائد على الساقي، ومعنى ذكر ربه: ذكر يوسف لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's whisper distracted the cupbearer until he forgot Joseph's request; God prolonged Joseph's imprisonment to increase his reward.
rows.anchor: وإنساء الشيطان له بما يوسوس إليه من اشتغاله حتى يذهل عما قال له يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A few years is left vague; reports give seven or twelve, or count seven after the prisoners left or two years, while the apparent sense is Joseph's full prison term.
rows.anchor: وبضع سنين مجمل، فقيل: سبع، وقيل: اثنا عشر. والظاهر أن قوله: فلبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some make the pronoun in أنساه refer to Joseph and build stories on that reading that Abū Ḥayyān says should not be attributed to prophets.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في أنساه عائد على يوسف. ورتبوا على ذلك أخبارا لا تليق نسبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egyptian king, named al-Rayyān ibn al-Walīd, sees seven fat cows from a dry river swallowed by seven lean cows, and seven ripe green ears overpowered by seven dry ones.
rows.anchor: لما دنا فرج يوسف عليه السلام رأى ملك مصر الريان بن الوليد رؤيا عجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense أرى recounts a scene as if occurring now; أفتوني في رؤياي shows it is a dream.
rows.anchor: وأرى حكاية حال، فلذلك جاء بالمضارع دون رأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samān modifies the cows rather than the numeral, distinguishing a kind of cow; modifying the number itself would wrongly imply that the seven were fat.
rows.anchor: وسمان صفة لقوله: بقرات، ميز العدد بنوع من البقرات وهي السمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between ثلاث رجال كرام and ثلاثة رجال كرام shows that describing the counted subset differs from describing the people as a whole.
rows.anchor: وفرق بين قولك: عندي ثلاث رجال كرام، وثلاثة رجال كرام، لأن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven is not annexed to the adjective ajāf because numerals normally annex to adjectives only in poetry; exceptions are adjectives used as nouns, such as knights or companions.
rows.anchor: ولم يضف سبع إلى عجاف لأن اسم العدد لا يضاف إلى الصفة إلا في الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of seven cows implies that the lean cows are also seven cows, with the counted noun omitted before their adjective.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله: سبع بقرات على أن السبع العجاف بقرات، كأنه قيل: سبع بقرات عجاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ajāf follows the opposite adjective samān, though the expected plural of ajfāʾ is ʿujuf, like khudr for khadrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وجاء جمع عجفاء على عجاف، وقياسه عجف كخضراء أو خضر، حملا على سمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division between fat and lean cows implies seven ears in each division; the numeral is omitted before أخر يابسات.
rows.anchor: والتقسيم في البقرات يقتضي التقسيم في السنبلات، فيكون قد حذف اسم العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخر cannot be a genitive adjective of سنبلات خضر, since being another set makes it separate from the seven it would otherwise modify.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون وأخر مجرورا عطفا على سنبلات خضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ are the king's leading officials who attend him.
rows.anchor: والملأ: أشراف دولته وأعيانهم الذين يحضرون عند الملك

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar assimilates the hamza in ruʾyā through an unusual sequence of sound changes; grammarians call it irregular because the waw substitution is optional.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: بالإدغام في الرؤيا، وبابه بعد قلب الهمزة واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in للرؤيا strengthens the verb's access to its object when the object precedes; it does not work as well when the object follows.
rows.anchor: واللام في الرؤيا مقوية لوصول الفعل إلى مفعوله إذا تقدم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes تعبرون the predicate of كنتم.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن خبر كنتم هو قوله: تعبرون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers three more complex parses: الرؤيا as an explanatory topic with an omitted object, as predicate of كان with another predicate or circumstantial phrase, or as governed by an understood verb meaning undertake interpretation.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري فيه وجوها متكلفة أحدها: أن تكون الرؤيا للبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dream interpretation is called عبور by analogy with crossing a river, as the interpreter reaches the vision's final meaning.
rows.anchor: وعبارة الرؤيا مأخوذة من عبر النهر إذا جازه من شط إلى شط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḍghāth is plural of ḍighth, a confused mixture of dreams from inner thoughts, Satanic whispering, or human temperament; the word originally described mixed plants.
rows.anchor: وأضغاث جمع ضغث أي تخاليط أحلام، وهي ما يكون من حديث النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king's single vision can be called plural dreams because it contains multiple things, as a generic plural, or because he recounted other dreams with it.
rows.anchor: وأن رؤياه واحدة إما باعتبار متعلقاتها إذ هي أشياء، وإما باعتبار جواز ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أضغاث أحلام is a predicate with an omitted subject, meaning these are confused dreams.
rows.anchor: والأحلام جمع حلم، وأضغاث خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي: هي أضغاث أحلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that the officials deny being able to interpret dreams at all.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنهم نفوا عن أنفسهم العلم بتأويل الأحلام أي: لسنا من أهل تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they deny knowledge only of confused, false dreams, which have no interpretation; this need not mean they cannot interpret a sound vision or claim expertise.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الأحلام المنفي علمها أرادوا بها الموصوفة بالتخليط والأباطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem cited by al-Mubarrad illustrates the use of the ungeminated verb ʿabara for interpreting a dream.
rows.anchor: رأيت رؤيا ثم عبرتها ... وكنت للأحلام عبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the dream stumped the king's court, the cupbearer remembered Joseph and his own and companion's interpretations after a long interval; أمّة means a long period and the clause is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: لما استثنى الملك في رؤياه وأعضل على الملأ تأويلها، تذكر الناجي من القتل وهو ساقي الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading ادكر derives from اذْتكر by changing and assimilating consonants; al-Ḥasan reads واذكر with a different assimilation.
rows.anchor: وادكر أي تذكر ما سبق له مع يوسف بعد أمة أي: مدة طويلة. والجملة من قوله وادكر حالية

rows.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads after immah with kasra on the hamza, meaning after the blessing of surviving execution.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي: بعد إمة بكسر الهمزة أي: بعد نعمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains the blessing as God drawing Joseph near to release and cites a poem using immah for blessing or good fortune.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: بعد نعمة أنعم الله بها على يوسف في تقريب إطلاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yughāth may derive from rescue and relief or from rain; an Arab woman says the latter form when asking for rain.
rows.anchor: يغاث: يحتمل أن يكون من الغوث وهو الفرج، يقال: أغاثهم الله فرج عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭb is a consequential matter or affair, plural khuṭūb; a poetic line illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: الخطب: الشأن والأمر الذي فيه خطر، ويجمع على خطوب قال: وما المرء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl explains ḥaṣḥaṣa as becoming clear after being hidden.
rows.anchor: حصحص تبين بعد الخفاء، قاله الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other lexical explanations derive ḥaṣḥaṣ from the share allotted to truth over falsehood, or from a camel settling firmly on its knees.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مأخوذ من الحصة حصحص الحق بانت حصته من حصة الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jihāz means travelers' provisions and equipment, anything carried, a bride's trousseau, or what is needed to bury the dead.
rows.anchor: الجهاز: ما يحتاج إليه المسافر من زاد ومتاع، وكل ما يحمل، وجهاز العروس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-raḥl is the load on a riding animal; riḥāl is its common plural and arḥul its less common plural.
rows.anchor: الرحل: ما على ظهر المركوب من متاع الراكب أو غيره، وجمعه رحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māra and amāra mean to bring useful goods or provisions, called mīra; a poem uses the word for provisioning.
rows.anchor: مار يمير، وأمار يمير، إذا جلب الخير وهي الميرة قال: بعثتك مائرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿīr generally means a male camel, but can refer to a camel of either sex; its bāʾ may take kasra, and its small and large plurals are أبعرة and بعران.
rows.anchor: البعير في الأشهر الجمل مقابل الناقة، وقد يطلق على الناقة، كما يطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immah with fatḥa on hamza means blessing or a good condition; readers transmit forms with an open hamza, a light mīm, or a still mīm.
rows.anchor: أعلم: الأمة النعمة، والحال الحسنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن علي والضحاك وقتادة وأبو رجاء وشبيل بن عزرة وربيعة بن عمرو
rows.claim: These readers use after ummah with fatḥa on hamza, a light mīm, and hāʾ; similar readings are variously reported from Ibn ʿUmar, Mujāhid, and ʿIkrima.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، وزيد بن علي، والضحاك، وقتادة، وأبو رجاء، وشبيل بن عزرة الضبعي، وربيعة بن عمرو: بعد أمه

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد وشبيل بن عزرة
rows.claim: They also read ummah with a still mīm as an irregular verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وأيضا مجاهد، وشبيل بن عزرة: بعد أمه بسكون الميم، مصدر أمه على غير قياس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the still-mīm reading an error; Abū Ḥayyān objects that he habitually labels readings erroneous.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومن قرأ بسكون الميم فقد أخطأ انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer says he will report the interpretation from someone who possesses its knowledge, not from himself.
rows.anchor: أنا أنبئكم بتأويله أي أخبركم به عمن عنده علمه لا من جهتي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads أنا أتيكم, from the verb meaning to come, as also found in the codex.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن أنا أتيكم مضارع أتى من الإتيان، وكذا في الإمام

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's codex adds فأرسلون, meaning send me to Joseph and allow me to ask for an interpretation.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي: فأرسلون، أي ابعثوني إليه لأسأله، ومروني باستعباره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Joseph's prison was outside the king's city; another report places it inside the city, with a present-day site identified by the Nile eight miles from Fusṭāṭ.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كان في السجن في غير مدينة الملك، وقيل: كان فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative elides the dispatch and arrival: the king sends the cupbearer to Joseph, who then addresses him.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف التقدير: فأرسلوه إلى يوسف فأتاه فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq is an intensive form; the cupbearer calls Joseph that after knowing him for a long time and testing his truthfulness in both dream interpretations.
rows.anchor: والصديق بناء مبالغة كالشريب والسكير، وكان قد صحبه زمانا وجرب صدقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer hopes to return with the interpretation, but says perhaps because he might die before reaching the king.
rows.anchor: وقوله: لعلي أرجع إلى الناس أي: بتفسير هذه الرؤيا. واحترز بلفظة لعلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the hope to return explains the aim of asking for interpretation: the court may recognize Joseph's learning and release him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لعلهم يعلمون فضلك ومكانك من العلم، فيطلبونك ويخلصونك من محنتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's reply combines three kinds of speech: interpretation by meaning rather than wording, practical advice, and a report of the unseen future eighth year.
rows.anchor: والثالث: الإعلام بالغيب في أمر العام الثامن، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the prediction of the eighth year as foreknowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: والثالث: الإعلام بالغيب في أمر العام الثامن، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows that this need not be unseen knowledge: the dream's interpretation itself implied hardship would end after seven years, followed by abundance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويحتمل هذا أن لا يكون غيبا، بل علم العبارة أعطى انقطاع الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of تزرعون is a prediction that they will farm continuously for seven years, aided by irrigation.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: تزرعون سبع سنين دأبا خبر، أخبر أنهم تتوالى لهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads تزرعون as an imperative phrased as a report to intensify the obligation to carry it out.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: تزرعون خبر في معنى الأمر كقوله: تؤمنون بالله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to store the harvest in its husk does not make the earlier verb an imperative; it is a forecast of seven successive crops followed by advice.
rows.anchor: ولا يدل الأمر بتركه في سنبله على أن تزرعون في معنى ازرعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾban means continuous diligence or one's usual practice in farming.
rows.anchor: ومعنى دأبا: ملازمة، كعادتكم في المزارعة

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads dāʾban with a fatḥa on hamza; the majority leave the hamza still, and both forms are verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص: دأبا بفتح الهمزة، والجمهور بإسكانها، وهما مصدران لدأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān derives the accusative from an omitted verb of the same root; al-Mubarrad instead connects it to تزرعون with the sense of working diligently, and another view treats it as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: وانتصابه بفعل محذوف من لفظه أي: تدابون دأبا، فهو منصوب على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in فما حصدتم can be conditional or relative.
rows.anchor: وما في قوله: فما حصدتم شرطية أو موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Storing grain in its husk preserves Egypt's wheat, which otherwise will not last two years; they should eat only what is necessary and consume the oldest stores first.
rows.anchor: فذروه في سنبله إشارة برأي نافع بحسب طعام مصر وحنطتها التي لا تبقى

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī reads يأكلون in the third person, meaning people will eat, rather than addressing the listeners.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: مما يأكلون بالياء على الغيبة أي: يأكل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase seven severe ones omits the word years, understood from the preceding seven years.
rows.anchor: وحذف المميز في قوله: سبع شداد أي: سبع سنين شداد، لدلالة قوله: سبع سنين عليه
